title: Спор на чаевые  (A Bet on the Tips)

segments.t: At the bar, the waiters divide up the evening's shared tip pool, and arrogant waiter Ilya complains that Max is getting an equal share after putting in less money.
Чаевые разбираем?
Сегодня по семь тысяч. Не густо.
Мне дали пятнашку, а я должен забрать семь?
Почему я должен работать на ушастых?
Чего? Я не работаю?
Я тоже в общую кассу положил.
Нормально устроился?
Все работают, не ты один.
Всё. До свидания.
Рыжий, погоди.
Спорим на все чаевые за смену?
Легко! Победитель потом заберёт всю сумму.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Чаевые разбираем?
'Are we dividing up the tips?' The grammar packs 'tips' and 'are dividing up' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Сегодня по семь тысяч. Не густо.
'Seven thousand each today. Not much.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'tonight' before landing on 'thickly'. Ilya answers right away.
Мне дали пятнашку, а я должен забрать семь?
'They gave me fifteen, and I have to take seven?' Notice how Russian expresses 'to me' and 'seven' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Почему я должен работать на ушастых?
'Why do I have to work for big-eared rookies?' The meaning hinges on 'why' working together with 'big-eared' in spoken Russian.
Чего? Я не работаю?
'What? Do I not work?' Notice how Russian expresses 'what' and 'work' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Я тоже в общую кассу положил.
'I also put money into the common pool.' Max brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'also' in a few short words.
Нормально устроился?
'You have arranged things nicely for yourself, haven't you?' The grammar packs 'normally' and 'got settled' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Все работают, не ты один.
'Everyone works, not just you alone.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'all' before landing on 'one'.
Всё. До свидания.
'That is all. Goodbye.' Notice how Russian expresses 'everything' and 'goodbye' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Рыжий, погоди.
'Redhead, wait.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'redhead' before landing on 'to wait a little'.
Спорим на все чаевые за смену?
'Shall we bet all the tips for the shift?' Notice how Russian expresses 'let's bet' and 'shift' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Max answers right away.
Легко! Победитель потом заберёт всю сумму.

'Easy! The winner will take the whole sum afterward.' Max anchors the line on 'easily', while 'sum' completes the thought. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
